name: Novo Nordisk A/S

thesisState.summary: Novo Nordisk remains a high-priority portfolio research case after the 2026 pricing/competition reset. Deep Dive and valuation input scaffold are complete; the key unresolved decision is whether PM assumptions support a full valuation model.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Evidence that US realised price pressure is worse/better than current guidance implies.
Oral Wegovy uptake, persistence and channel mix differ materially from assumptions.
Lilly/tirzepatide competitive pressure changes Novo's volume share trajectory.
CagriSema, semaglutide 7.2 mg or other pipeline decisions materially alter long-term obesity share/margin outlook.

businessSnapshot.description: Global healthcare company focused on diabetes, obesity and rare disease, with core economics driven by GLP-1 therapies including Ozempic and Wegovy.
businessSnapshot.cycleExposure: Healthcare/pharma; less macro-cyclical than industrials, but exposed to pricing, reimbursement, regulation, patent cycles and competitive clinical data.

keyDrivers: Global GLP-1 volume expansion in obesity and diabetes.
Wegovy and oral Wegovy uptake, access and channel mix.
Ozempic durability in diabetes despite market share pressure.
US realised prices, rebates, Medicaid/coverage and MFN effects.
Manufacturing capacity expansion and gross margin recovery.
Pipeline optionality: CagriSema, semaglutide 7.2 mg, zenagamtide/amycretin, cardiovascular/metabolic assets.
keyRisks: 2026 adjusted sales and operating profit guidance implies decline at CER due to lower realised prices and competition.
US Operations pressure from pricing, coverage changes and competition.
Global diabetes value share declined in 2025.
Gross margin pressure from Catalent-site depreciation/amortisation, restructuring and capacity expansion costs.
Patent/compound expiry impacts for semaglutide in certain International Operations markets.
Execution risk in scaling supply chain and launching oral Wegovy.
watchMetrics: Obesity care sales growth and branded GLP-1 obesity volume share.
Wegovy prescription trends, including oral Wegovy launch metrics.
Ozempic sales growth and GLP-1 diabetes value share.
US vs International Operations sales growth.
Gross margin and operating margin bridge, including restructuring/Catalent effects.
Free cash flow after high CAPEX.
Management guidance revisions for adjusted sales/operating profit growth.
openQuestions: What is the normalised 2027-2030 revenue/margin trajectory after 2026 pricing reset?
How much oral Wegovy is incremental vs cannibalising injectable Wegovy/GLP-1 demand?
What share and price assumptions are required for Novo to defend premium valuation vs Lilly?
How should we adjust margins for restructuring, Catalent integration and capacity ramp costs?
What is the probability-weighted value of CagriSema, semaglutide 7.2 mg and next-generation assets?

recentEvents.summary: Novo Nordisk reported 2025 sales of DKK 309.064bn (+6% reported, +10% CER) and operating profit of DKK 127.658bn (-1% reported, +6% CER). 2026 adjusted sales and adjusted operating profit growth guidance: -5% to -13% at CER.
US FDA approved once-daily oral semaglutide 25 mg for obesity under Wegovy pill; launched 5 January 2026 with around 50,000 weekly prescriptions as of 23 January, per company announcement.

Q1 2026 investor presentation: adjusted sales DKK 70.063bn (-4% CER) and adjusted operating profit DKK 32.858bn (-6% CER); outlook raised to adjusted sales and adjusted operating profit growth of -4% to -12% CER, driven by higher GLP-1 expectations. Wegovy pill reached >1m US patients since launch and ~207k weekly TRx as of 17 Apr 2026.
sources: Novo Nordisk Q1 2026 Investor Presentation, pp. 4, 6, 10-11
